extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent applicants, attorneys, and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing and processing continuation, continuation‑in‑part, continued prosecution (CPA), substitute/refile applications, and claiming the benefit of earlier U.S. or provisional filing dates under 35 U.S.C. 120, 119(e) and 37 C.F.R. 1.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) eligibility and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA may only be filed in a design application. A CPA cannot be filed in a utility or plant application. A CPA must be filed prior to payment of the issue fee unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c) is granted in the prior application. The prior application identified must be a design application that is complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b). A continuation-in-part (C‑I‑P) cannot be filed as a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may consider filing a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 in utility or plant applications. Filing a CPA is construed to include an express abandonment of the prior application as of the CPA filing date. Filing a CPA will be construed to include a waiver of confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent permitted by 37 CFR 1.14. In a CPA, no reference to the prior application is needed in the first sentence of the specification and none should be submitted; if submitted it will not be entered. See MPEP § 706.07(h) and form PTO/SB/30 for RCE information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO/SB/29 (CPA Request Transmittal) required contents and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/29 is the Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) Request Transmittal for design applications. The form includes fields such as prior application number, filing date, title, attorney docket number, first named inventor, examiner name, art unit, express statements about continuation/divisional/CPA, check boxes for duplicate, small entity status, fee payments, deposit account authorizations, requests for suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103(b)), correspondence address, and signature of applicant/attorney/agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: Information on the form may become public; do not include credit card information on this form (use PTO-2038). The collection of information is required by 37 CFR 1.53(d); estimated time to complete ~24 minutes. If assistance is needed, call USPTO help. The filing of this CPA is a request to expressly abandon the prior application; use 37 CFR 1.53(b) to file a continuation, divisional, or C‑I‑P of an application that is not to be abandoned. The prior application’s correspondence address will carry over unless a new address is provided. Signature of applicant/attorney/agent is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt for facsimile transmitted CPA (Form PTO/SB/29A) handling and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/29A is the Receipt for Facsimile Transmitted CPA and, if included, will be date stamped and mailed to the address in item 1. By this receipt, the USPTO (a) acknowledges that a request for a CPA in a design application was filed by facsimile transmission on the date stamped and (b) verifies only that the application number provided on the receipt matches the application number on the accompanying request for a CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This receipt CANNOT be used to acknowledge receipt of any papers other than the request for a CPA. USPTO handling instructions: stamp date of complete transmission and include the organization name providing the stamp; verify application numbers; if inconsistent, strike through and insert correct number if possible, then mail. The collection of information is required by 37 CFR 1.8; estimated time ~24 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for notifying applicants of CPA defects or status
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific USPTO notice forms are used by Technology Centers to notify applicants of defects or status relating to applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d). These include: 'Notice of Improper CPA (or FWC) Filing For Utility or Plant Applications Filed Before June 8, 1995' (Form PTO-2011); 'Notice of Improper CPA For Design Applications' (Form PTO-2012); 'Notice To File Missing Parts Of Application (CPA), For Design Applications' (Form PTO-2021); 'Notice Of Incomplete Reply (CPA) For Design Applications' (Form PTO-2018); and 'Notice Of Abandonment Under 37 CFR 1.53(f) (CPA) For Design Applications' (Form PTO-2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms are used to communicate specific defects (improper filing, missing parts, incomplete reply) or abandonment under CPA rules. See the individual form captions and MPEP references for form-specific wording and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation application definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation is a second application for the same invention claimed in a prior nonprovisional application and filed before the original prior application becomes abandoned or patented. The continuation may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or 1.53(d) if a design application). The applicant in the continuation must include at least one inventor named in the prior nonprovisional application. The disclosure in the continuation must be the same as that of the original application (i.e., the continuation should not include anything which would constitute new matter). The continuation must claim the benefit of the prior nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application claiming the benefit of a provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) should not be called a 'continuation' of the provisional. Filing a continuation allows introduction of a new set of claims and further examination by the primary examiner. For notation in the file history by the examiner in the case of a continuation, see MPEP § 202.02. Use form paragraph 2.05 to remind applicant of possible continuation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation‑in‑part (C‑I‑P) application definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation-in-part is an application filed during the lifetime of an earlier nonprovisional application, repeating some substantial portion or all of the earlier application and adding matter not disclosed in the earlier application. The continuation-in-part may only be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). The C‑I‑P must claim the benefit of the prior nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 365(c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuation-in-part CANNOT be filed as a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d). An application claiming the benefit of a provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) should not be called a 'continuation-in-part' of the provisional. The mere filing of a C‑I‑P does not itself create a presumption that the applicant acquiesces in any rejections outstanding in the copending national nonprovisional application. For the alleged C‑I‑P to derive the benefit of the earlier filing date, it must meet other requirements of 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78, such as: (A) common inventor(s); (B) filed before patenting/abandonment/termination of proceedings on the first application; and (C) contains or is amended to contain a specific reference to the earlier filed application (submitted in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76(b)(5)). See MPEP § 201.11 and form paragraph 2.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute application definition and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Substitute' designates an application that is in essence the duplicate of an application by the same applicant abandoned before the filing of the later application. Current practice does not require applicant to insert in the specification reference to the earlier application; attention should be called to the earlier application. A 'Substitute' does not obtain the benefit of the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notation in the file history that one application is a 'Substitute' for another is printed in the heading of the patent copies. See MPEP § 202.02. Use form paragraph 2.07 to remind applicant of possible substitute status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the term 'Refile' and required correction to 'Substitute'
rubrics_metrics.description: No official definition has been given to the term 'Refile,' though it is sometimes used as an alternative for the term 'Substitute.' If the applicant designates the application as 'Refile' and the examiner finds the application is a duplicate of a former application abandoned prior to filing the second application, the examiner should require substitution of the word 'substitute' for 'refile' since the former term has official recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.08 to remind applicant of possible refile status and to require appropriate corrections if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application may be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of a prior nonprovisional or provisional application if certain statutory and regulatory conditions are met. Under 35 U.S.C. 120, the invention must be disclosed in the manner provided by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 in the earlier application, be filed before patenting/abandonment/termination of proceedings on the first application, and contain or be amended to contain a specific reference to the earlier filed application. Under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), a nonprovisional application claiming benefit of a provisional must be filed not later than 12 months after the provisional filing date and must contain or be amended to contain a specific reference to the provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may consider failure to timely submit the specific reference as waiver of benefit, and may establish procedures (including surcharge) to accept unintentionally delayed submissions. 37 CFR 1.78 requires that, to claim benefit of prior-filed copending nonprovisional or international applications: (a)(1) each prior-filed application must name at least one inventor named in the later application and disclose the named inventor’s invention in the manner of 35 U.S.C. 112 ¶1; and (2)(i) each prior-filed application must be either an international application entitled to a filing date under PCT Article 11 and designating the U.S., or entitled to a filing date under § 1.53(b) or (d) and have paid the basic filing fee under § 1.16 within the pendency of the application. Except for CPAs under § 1.53(d), any nonprovisional or international application claiming benefit must contain or be amended to contain a reference to each prior application identifying it by application number or international application number and filing date and indicating relationship of the applications. See MPEP § 201.11 for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: File history notation for continuation and continuation-in-part status
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should place notation in the file history when an application may be a continuation or a continuation-in-part so that the file reflects the relationship to the prior application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For notation procedures and how such notations appear in the file history or on patent copies, see MPEP § 202.02. Use the specified form paragraphs (e.g., 2.05 for continuation, 2.06 for C‑I‑P) to remind applicants of possible status and to record necessary information.
